newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA UNVEILS AMBITIOUS TOURISM PLANS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA UNVEILS AMBITIOUS TOURISM PLANS.

text.p: South Africa wants to nearly double tourism's contribution to its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to 8.0 percent by the year 2000, Tourism and Environmental Affairs Minister Pallo Jordan said on Tuesday.
Jordan told parliament that one of the hurdles to boosting tourism was the perception that South Africa was not safe.
"The department is currently awarding tenders for a professional communications campaign to rectify wrong perceptions," he said.

Jordan said the three-year targets involved in increasing tourism's GDP contribution from the present 4.5 percent included boosting foreign exchange earnings by an average of 15 percent a year to 23 billion rand a year.

It was hoped that foreign tourist numbers would increase 17 percent a year to 2.2 million and that the number of sustainable jobs in the industry would rise to 860,000 in 2000 from 550,000 now, he added.
Jordan said South Africa's promotion efforts would concentrate on the type of tourist who would spend more than 7,000 rand per visit.
